inputs.instruction: Read the following files and report their exact export signatures and key logic: project/src/entities/taskDefinition.js, project/src/entities/taskInstance.js, project/src/context.js. Also read SPEC §4.1 (ScheduleComputer, lines 176-198) from project/family-task-manager-spec.md. Report file paths and line ranges.

Create one new file for Phase 2 of the Family Task Manager. JavaScript ESM. before: null (new file).

File — project/src/modules/scheduleComputer.js:
Export scheduleComputer(taskDef, referenceTime, options) per SPEC §4.1.

Signature:
  scheduleComputer(taskDef, referenceTime, options = {})
  -> TaskInstance[]

Where:
  taskDef: a TaskDefinition JSON-LD object (from createTaskDefinition)
  referenceTime: ISO-8601 string
  options.lookAheadSeconds: number (default 604800 = 7 days)

Dependencies:
  import { RRule } from 'rrule';
  import { createTaskInstance } from '../entities/taskInstance.js';

Rules (SPEC §4.1):
1. If scheduleType === 'one-time':
   - If dueAt['@value'] <= referenceTime: return []
   - Else: return [createTaskInstance({ taskDefinitionId: taskDef['@id'], assignedTo: taskDef['ftm:assignedTo'], dueAt: taskDef['ftm:schedule']['ftm:dueAt']['@value'] })]

2. If scheduleType === 'recurring':
   - Try to parse recurrenceRule. On any parse error, return a result array with result['ftm:error'] = 'invalid-rrule' (attach to the array object, per operator I3 resolution). Use try/catch around RRule.fromString().
   - Create the RRule: RRule.fromString(recurrenceRule) — note rrule v3 parses DTSTART from the rule string or accepts dtstart option. Set dtstart from recurrenceStart: const rule = new RRule({ ...RRule.parseString(recurrenceRule), dtstart: new Date(taskDef['ftm:schedule']['ftm:recurrenceStart']) });
   - Enumerate occurrences in window (referenceTime, referenceTime + lookAheadSeconds]:
     const start = new Date(referenceTime);
     const end = new Date(new Date(referenceTime).getTime() + lookAheadSeconds * 1000);
     const dates = rule.between(start, end, true); // inclusive upper bound
     Filter out any date exactly equal to start (to satisfy open-start SPEC convention).
   - Return dates.map(d => createTaskInstance({ taskDefinitionId: taskDef['@id'], assignedTo: taskDef['ftm:assignedTo'], dueAt: d.toISOString() }))
   - If no occurrences: return []

3. All returned instances must have completionState.status: 'pending' and reminderSummary.totalSent: 0 (guaranteed by createTaskInstance defaults).

4. Function must be pure: no I/O, no side effects. Calling twice with same args produces same logical output (UUIDs will differ — that is acceptable).

Edge cases:
- If recurrenceRule is null/empty string and scheduleType is 'recurring', treat as invalid-rrule.
- lookAheadSeconds defaults to 604800 when options is omitted or options.lookAheadSeconds is undefined.

File 1 — project/src/modules/taskListComputer.js:
Export taskListComputer(instances, filter) per SPEC §4.4.
Returns TaskInstance[] — filtered and sorted. Pure function; does not mutate input.

filter shape: { assignedTo?: string, status?: 'pending'|'completed', fromDate?: string, toDate?: string }

Rules (SPEC §4.4):
1. Filter by assignedTo if present: keep instances where instance['ftm:assignedTo'] === filter.assignedTo
2. Filter by status if present: keep instances where instance['ftm:completionState']['ftm:status'] === filter.status
3. Filter by fromDate if present: keep instances where instance['ftm:dueAt']['@value'] >= filter.fromDate
4. Filter by toDate if present: keep instances where instance['ftm:dueAt']['@value'] <= filter.toDate
5. Sort by ftm:dueAt['@value'] ascending (string ISO-8601 comparison works correctly)
6. Tiebreak for equal dueAt: pending before completed
   (sort pending first: if a.dueAt === b.dueAt and a is pending and b is completed, a comes first)

File 2 — project/src/modules/recurrenceMaterializer.js:
Export recurrenceMaterializer(taskDefs, existingInstances, currentTime, options) per SPEC §4.5.
Returns { toCreate: TaskInstance[], skipped: number }. Pure function.

import { scheduleComputer } from './scheduleComputer.js';

options shape: { lookAheadSeconds?: number, catchUpPolicy?: 'all'|'current-only' }
Defaults: lookAheadSeconds = 604800, catchUpPolicy = 'current-only'

Rules (SPEC §4.5):
1. For each taskDef in taskDefs where taskDef['ftm:schedule']['ftm:scheduleType'] === 'recurring':
   a. // FIXME: catchUpWindowSeconds not defined in SPEC §4.5 rule 1a — using 604800s (7 days) as operator-confirmed default (I9).
      const catchUpWindowSeconds = options.catchUpWindowSeconds ?? 604800;
      const lookAheadSeconds = options.lookAheadSeconds ?? 604800;
      const windowStart = new Date(new Date(currentTime).getTime() - catchUpWindowSeconds * 1000).toISOString();
      const candidates = scheduleComputer(taskDef, windowStart, { lookAheadSeconds: catchUpWindowSeconds + lookAheadSeconds });
      // Handle invalid-rrule: if candidates['ftm:error'], skip this definition.
   b. Deduplicate: remove any candidate whose dueAt matches an existing instance
      (match by taskDef['@id'] === existingInstance['ftm:taskDefinition'] AND candidate dueAt === existingInstance['ftm:dueAt']['@value'])
   c. If catchUpPolicy === 'current-only': further filter out candidates where dueAt < currentTime; increment skipped for each filtered.
   d. Append remaining to toCreate.
2. Return { toCreate, skipped }.

No I/O. No mutation of inputs.
